newsitem.title: USA: Nu-Kote says judge rules against Hewlett-Packard.
newsitem.headline: Nu-Kote says judge rules against Hewlett-Packard.

text.p: A federal judge ruled that Hewlett-Packard Co. falsely labels packages for its inkjet cartridges to make consumers believe replacements are incompatible with Hewlett-Packard printers, cartridge rival Nu-Kote International Inc. said Sunday.

In his ruling Friday in San Jose, Calif., U.S. District Judge James Ware forbade computer industry giant Hewlett-Packard from falsely labeling its inkjet cartridge packaging, Nu-Kote said in a news release.

The ruling stemmed from a motion filed in March by Nu-Kote, a Dallas-based supplier of inkjet replacement cartridges, seeking to stop Hewlett-Packard from making changes to its inkjet cartridges, saying it unfairly restricts competition.
A spokesman for Palo Alto, Calif.-based Hewlett-Packard was not available to comment.
The cartridges contain the ink used in inkjet computer printers.
Nu-Kote is a competitor of Palo-Alto, Calif.,-based Hewlett-Packard for the sale of the Hewlett-Packard cartridges, which Nu-Kote refills for reuse.

According to Nu-Kote, Ware ruled that Hewlett-Packard's packaging for its two most popular inkjet cartridges is "literally false" because while the company's packaging contains cartridges for which Nu-Kote currently offers a compatible replacement, it depicts a cartridge that is not useable by Nu-Kote customers.
Nu-Kote said the judge agreed with it that Hewlett-Packard's packaging hides this fact and issued an order stating, "HP shall be enjoined from using its false packaging."

Nu-Kote's motion for an injunction is part of litigation between the two companies. Hewlett Packard originally sued Nu-Kote for patent infringement. Nu-Kote filed a counterclaim based on antitrust grounds.
Nu-Kote said the court has set a hearing for July 23 to specify exact terms of the injunction, including the effective date and termination date.
The company said that at a later date a jury trial will determine the amount of damages to be awarded to it.
